analysis.summary: Historical JumpThreading bug fix: floating-point Eq/Ne comparisons must not be folded through integer ScalarInt/bit-pattern comparisons; this was the fix for issue #128243, backported as “Disable jump threading of float equality #128271”.
analysis.originalLogic: Before the fix, `process_assign` handled `BinOp::Eq` by selecting `ScalarInt::TRUE` and `BinOp::Ne` by selecting `ScalarInt::FALSE`, then normalized the encountered constant and called `value.const_.normalize(self.tcx, self.param_env).try_to_scalar_int()?` to construct `Condition`s. There was no floating-point type check, so f32/f64 constants flowed into this integer/ScalarInt path.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historically incorrect transformation was to let JumpThreading reason about floating-point `Eq`/`Ne` as if equality followed the constant’s integer ScalarInt/bit pattern. That is semantically wrong: `-0.0` and `+0.0` are equal as floats but have different bits, while NaN is unequal to itself even when the bit pattern matches. The fix returns `None` for any floating-point constant before `try_to_scalar_int`, disabling this folding.
analysis.inputDomain: Rust MIR bool assignments/conditions generated from source comparisons `x == C` or `x != C` where the compared value/constant is `f32` or `f64`, reached by JumpThreading’s `process_assign`. The important inputs include `-0.0`, `+0.0`, and NaN, not only ordinary finite floats.
analysis.trigger: `process_assign` sees a `BinOp::Eq` or `BinOp::Ne` with an available constant condition, maps it to `ScalarInt::TRUE` or `ScalarInt::FALSE`, and—before the fix—reaches `try_to_scalar_int()` without rejecting a floating-point constant.
preconditions: JumpThreading is run on MIR containing a floating-point equality or inequality against a constant.
The comparison is in a form where `process_assign` can otherwise build jump-threading conditions.
To expose the semantic error, use `-0.0 == 0.0` or a same-bit-pattern NaN comparison.
pitfalls: Do not replace floating-point `Eq`/`Ne` with ScalarInt or bit-pattern equality.
`-0.0 == 0.0` is true even though their bit patterns differ.
NaN compares unequal even when the same NaN bit pattern is compared with itself, so bitwise equality is also wrong for NaN.
The safe fix rejects all floating-point constants in this Eq/Ne path rather than special-casing only zero or NaN.
The regression test must assert that a relevant `switchInt` remains; the diff legitimately removes the earlier `if true` switchInt, so check the right function and remaining comparison.
analysis.testStrategy: Add a focused `tests/mir-opt/jump_threading.rs` regression function such as `fn floats() -> u32 { let x = if true { -0.0 } else { 1.0 }; if x == 0.0 { 0 } else { 1 } }`, with `// CHECK-LABEL: fn floats(`, `// CHECK: switchInt(`, a call from `main`, and `// EMIT_MIR jump_threading.floats.JumpThreading.diff` (the historical patch generated both `panic-abort` and `panic-unwind` diffs). Supplement with a runtime `assert_eq!(floats(), 0)` and optionally a NaN/`!=` variant to guard both special cases. Verify that JumpThreading does not turn the float comparison into an unconditional branch.
evidence: Disable jump threading of float equality #128271
Floating point equality does not follow bit-patterns.
-0.0 and NaN both have special rules for equality,
and therefore we cannot use integer comparisons for them.
// Test for issue #128243, where float equality was assumed to be bitwise.
// When adding float support, it must be ensured that this continues working properly.
